title: Pre-Market Brief — 18 Nov 2026
intro: US stock futures are pointing to a mixed open, led by strong gains in the Nasdaq 100 while the Russell 2000 lags in negative territory. Wall Street is digesting a flurry of high-profile corporate earnings, ongoing regulatory scrutiny surrounding Nvidia, and fresh monetary policy signaling from the Federal Reserve.

sections.heading: 🛢 Oil desk
sections.content: Crude oil is trading lower today, with WTI dropping 1.12% to 85.05 and Brent declining 0.59% to 89.84. The pullback in energy prices comes as broader risk-off flows in commodities and a firmer US dollar outweigh ongoing geopolitical developments.

sections.heading: Market theme
sections.content: Risk appetite remains bifurcated as mega-cap technology outperforms while broader market sentiment stays cautious amid elevated Treasury yields and a strengthening DXY at 103.75. Safe-haven demand and profit-taking are weighing heavily across commodities, with sharp liquidations hitting both precious and industrial metals.

sections.heading: Potential scenario
sections.content: The base case for the cash open is a continuation of tech-led outperformance targeting a hold above the S&P 500 futures level of 7,388.50. The alternative scenario involves broader macro headwinds and rate fears dragging indices lower toward a test of the Nasdaq 100 futures level of 27,301.

sections.heading: Key risks
sections.content:
- Hawkish Federal Reserve commentary and the release of afternoon FOMC meeting minutes
- Persistent downside pressure and volatility across global metal and energy commodity complexes
